name: Tiffany Koyama Lane

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Koyama Lane was elected District 3 city councilor in November 2024 and began her term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 3 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in the councilor's City of Portland page, re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked. The page says 'their term'; the same page lists Koyama Lane's pronouns as She/Her, so 'her' is correct.

bio.statement: Koyama Lane's City of Portland page describes her as an award-winning educator, fourth-generation Japanese American, mom and community organizer.
bio.excerpt: She is an award-winning educator, fourth‑generation Japanese American, mom, and community organizer

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in the councilor's City of Portland page, re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Koyama Lane taught at Sunnyside Environmental School before running for council.
bio.excerpt: Prior to her City Council run, Koyama Lane was a teacher at Sunnyside Environmental School.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Mercury (Mercury Election Strike Force, 2026-09-09), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

positions.statement: OPB reports Koyama Lane has spent her two years on council pushing for traffic safety and equity programs.
positions.excerpt: Koyama Lane has spent her two years in City Hall pushing for traffic safety, equity programs

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in OPB (Alex Zielinski, 2026-10-07), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Koyama Lane has said she won't vote for city funding for the Moda Center renovation unless the Trail Blazers ownership group contributes.
positions.excerpt: won’t vote to approve any city funding for the project if the Trail Blazers ownership group doesn’t chip in

verification.note: The original statement said only 'the project'. The Mercury's preceding sentence identifies it as the Moda Center renovation, so the statement now names it. The excerpt is unchanged and confirmed verbatim. Re-fetched 2026-10-14.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Koyama Lane says corporations that benefit from Portland's workforce should pay their fair share.
positions.excerpt: We also need to make sure that corporations that benefit from our amazing workforce pay their fair share

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Tribune (Hannah Seibold, 2026-10-13), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Koyama Lane says she consistently hears worries about affordability and cuts to public goods.
positions.excerpt: Affordability is a worry I hear consistently from Portlanders, as are the massive cuts to our public goods.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Tribune (Hannah Seibold, 2026-10-13), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

gaps: Voters' pamphlet statement not readable: the individual statement PDF in the county's Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide is a scan with no machine-readable text, and the full and large-print county pamphlet PDFs are cut off by the fetch tool (~105k characters) before the City of Portland section (pp. M-52 to M-66)
City filing form (AUD-120) PDF had no readable text
No campaign website found in a T1 source

verification_summary.balance_notes: Race portland-council-d3 (21 candidates). Every candidate was searched in the same shared sources: the Mercury (2026-09-09), OPB (2026-10-07), the Tribune Q&A (2026-10-13), the Multnomah pamphlet and the 2026 AUD-120 forms. The pamphlet index lists a statement for this candidate, but the collector could not read it. The pamphlet PDF text is 104,260 characters and ends before the Portland section (M-53 to M-60), and the individual statement scan is not linked from the MOO guide page and could not be re-fetched. This is a source-access gap, confirmed. The AUD-120 has no readable text. Koyama Lane has 3 bio and 4 position items. As an incumbent, a T1 council page was used. She states her pronouns as She/Her. The 'no council voting record' gap applies equally to all three incumbents. Incumbent=true confirmed (portland.gov/council lists her for District 3).
